reforms.description: The federal government committed to tying increased funding for researchers to objectives and conditions that will ensure greater diversity among the researcher population, as announced in the 2018 Budget.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Expanding the researcher talent pool by removing barriers to underrepresented groups increases human capital for innovation and research productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government committed to tying increased funding for researchers in its 2018 Budget to objectives and conditions that will ensure greater diversity among the researcher population.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant policy commitment to link public research funding to diversity objectives, addressing a structural barrier to human capital development in the research system. Affects the allocation of increased researcher funding but is narrower than a comprehensive research funding reform.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government also committed to tying increased funding for researchers in its 2018 Budget to objectives and conditions that will ensure greater diversity among the researcher population.

reforms.description: The PromoScience Program funds organisations that offer children of kindergarten or school age opportunities to participate in activities designed to build engagement, interest, skills and knowledge in STEM.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Building STEM engagement and skills among young people expands the future talent pipeline for research and innovation, supporting long-term human capital development.
reforms.status_evidence: The text refers to the PromoScience Program in present tense as an ongoing initiative that funds organisations.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted programme supporting STEM engagement among school-age children. While valuable for long-term human capital development, it is a narrowly focused initiative rather than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The PromoScience Program funds organisations that offer children of kindergarten or school age opportunities to participate in activities known to build engagement, interest, skills and knowledge in STEM.

reforms.description: The ChooseScience digital campaign, launched in February 2017, offers resources for parents and teachers to encourage young women to consider careers in STEM.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Removing gender barriers to STEM career participation expands the talent pool for research and innovation, increasing human capital productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The ChooseScience digital campaign was launched in February 2017.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted awareness and engagement campaign to encourage women into STEM careers. While addressing an important barrier, it is a communication initiative rather than a structural reform of research funding or institutions.
reforms.source_quote: The ChooseScience digital campaign, launched in February 2017, offers resources for parents and teachers to encourage young women to consider careers in STEM.

reforms.description: The federal government allocated CAD 400 million over three years for the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative to increase late-stage financing available to Canadian entrepreneurs.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increases access to late-stage venture capital for innovative firms, reducing financing constraints and enabling scaling of high-growth startups, which drives productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'CAD 400 million funding over three years for the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative' in the context of the 2018 federal budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant targeted intervention to address a specific market failure in late-stage venture financing for Canadian startups, with direct relevance to innovation and entrepreneurship.
reforms.source_quote: A positive step in this regard is the CAD 400 million funding over three years for the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative, which will increase late-stage financing available to Canadian entrepreneurs.

reforms.description: The 2018 federal budget allocated approximately CAD 650 million per year in additional funding for research and development, focused on fundamental research where market failures are most pervasive.
reforms.component_name: Additional R&D Funding for Fundamental Research
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public funding for fundamental research addresses market failures in basic science, building the knowledge foundation for long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'Around CAD 650 million per year in additional funding for research and development in the 2018 federal budget is focussed on fundamental research'.
reforms.importance_rationale: Substantial increase in public R&D funding directed at fundamental research, addressing a key market failure and supporting Canada's research capacity and long-term innovation potential.
reforms.source_quote: Around CAD 650 million per year in additional funding for research and development in the 2018 federal budget is focussed on fundamental research, where market failures are most pervasive.

reforms.description: The federal government allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional 'superclusters', designed to boost economic growth by complementing existing local strengths.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Regional innovation clusters leverage local strengths and facilitate knowledge spillovers, supporting the commercialisation and adoption of innovations across multiple sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has also allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional superclusters.
reforms.importance_rationale: Substantial allocation to regional innovation clusters with potential for broad economic impact. However, effectiveness depends on project selection and removal of barriers to innovation, as noted in the text.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government has also allocated CAD 950 million to accelerate innovation through five regional 'superclusters', which has the potential to boost economic growth through one-off funding that complements existing local strengths.

reforms.description: The Strategic Innovation Fund was established in 2017 to allocate repayable and non-repayable contributions to firms of all sizes across industrial and technology sectors, following a 2017 review of direct federal innovation programmes for business.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct grants and repayable contributions to firms support applied R&D and technology development, addressing capital market failures for innovative firms and improving allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: The Strategic Innovation Fund established in 2017 allocates repayable and non-repayable contributions to firms of all sizes across industrial and technology sectors.
reforms.importance_rationale: Represents a structural reform consolidating and restructuring direct federal innovation support for business. Shifts from tax-based to direct grant instruments and covers all firm sizes across multiple sectors, addressing long-standing OECD recommendations for more efficient targeting of business R&D support.
reforms.source_quote: All direct (non-tax) federal innovation programmes for business were reviewed in 2017 with changes including consolidation of programmes announced in Budget 2018. The Strategic Innovation Fund established in 2017 allocates repayable and non-repayable contributions to firms of all sizes across industrial and technology sectors.

reforms.description: Budget 2017 announced a review of the SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax credit programme to ensure its continued effectiveness and efficiency, with changes announced in Budget 2018.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The text indicates the SR&ED programme was reviewed for efficiency but does not specify the nature or direction of changes, making the growth impact ambiguous without additional detail.
reforms.status_evidence: Budget 2017 announced that the SR&ED program would be reviewed to ensure its continued effectiveness and efficiency. Changes were announced in Budget 2018.
reforms.importance_rationale: The SR&ED programme is a major instrument for indirect R&D support to firms. A review and restructuring represents a significant policy adjustment, though the specific changes are not detailed in this text.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2017 announced that the SR&ED program would be reviewed to ensure its continued effectiveness and efficiency. All direct (non-tax) federal innovation programmes for business were reviewed in 2017 with changes including consolidation of programmes announced in Budget 2018.

reforms.description: The Government of Canada committed to collecting better data and conducting rigorous cost-benefit evaluations of R&D support programmes, including the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP). Budget 2018 provided new funding to Statistics Canada and the Treasury Board Secretariat for this evaluation purpose.
reforms.package_name: 2017 Horizontal Review of Federal Business Innovation Programmes
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Rigorous evaluation of R&D support programmes improves allocative efficiency and ensures public innovation funding targets genuine market failures, enhancing overall innovation system productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Budget 2018 provided new funding to Statistics Canada and the Treasury Board Secretariat for evaluation purposes.
reforms.importance_rationale: Represents a significant governance improvement in the innovation support system by establishing rigorous evaluation mechanisms for major R&D programmes, though it is primarily a methodological reform rather than a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: As an outcome of the 2017 horizontal review of federal business innovation programmes, the Government of Canada will be collecting better data to be able to evaluate interventions in a robust manner, with new funding for this purpose provided in Budget 2018 to Statistics Canada and the Treasury Board Secretariat.

reforms.description: Budget 2017 provided CAD 221 million over five years (starting 2017–18) to fund work-integrated learning placements for Canadian post-secondary students through Mitacs, a not-for-profit organisation. The programme aims to scale up from 3,750 placements in 2017 to 10,000 annually, promoting entrepreneurial skills and STEM student engagement with industry.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Builds human capital for innovation by providing practical research and development experience to STEM graduates and strengthens university-industry knowledge transfer and collaboration.
reforms.status_evidence: Budget 2017 provided CAD 221 million over five years, starting in 2017–18, to provide work experience in businesses to Canadian post-secondary students.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant expansion of work-integrated learning capacity with substantial funding (CAD 221 million) and clear scaling targets (from 3,750 to 10,000 placements annually), strengthening the innovation ecosystem through human capital development.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2017 provided CAD 221 million over five years, starting in 2017–18, to provide work experience in businesses to Canadian post-secondary students, generally at the graduate-level. Funding is delivered by Mitacs, a not-for-profit organisation that builds partnerships between industry and educational institutions and has the goal of providing 10,000 work-integrated learning placements for Canadian post-secondary students and graduates each year—up from the 2017 level of 3,750 placements.

reforms.description: The Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) committed to investing CAD 200 million over 2018–19 to 2022–23 in women-led technology firms, scaling up business development support for growth-oriented female ventures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted venture capital support for women-led technology firms removes financing barriers to innovation and entrepreneurship, expanding the pool of innovative entrepreneurs and improving allocative efficiency in the startup ecosystem.
reforms.status_evidence: BDC has committed to investing CAD 200 million in women-led technology firms over 2018-19 to 2022-23.
reforms.importance_rationale: Represents a significant targeted intervention in the startup ecosystem with substantial funding (CAD 200 million) addressing a specific market gap in venture capital access for women entrepreneurs in technology sectors.
reforms.source_quote: BDC has committed to investing CAD 200 million in women-led technology firms over 2018-19 to 2022-23.
